cohort.clock: Earliest exact-head PR workflow creation to latest successful required check completion, not push-to-auto-merge readiness
cohort.sampling: Systematic chronological midpoint sample by newly opened devel-base PR day and path class; 6 production/3 fixtures per early day,12/6 on Nov15-16,2 per other class/day; no outcome filtering. Latest observed heads only; old PR pushes/superseded heads absent.
cohort.collection_clock_note: Conservative task observation envelope includes saved frame/check reads and final resampling. The final classification pass reused earlier raw responses; not an atomic snapshot.
limits: Systematic newly opened devel-base PR sample, balanced by day and path class. Latest observed heads only: older PRs receiving pushes and superseded heads absent. No outcome filtering; class distributions are unweighted, not a traffic census.

Frontend paths include agentplane/app/frontend. Production requires a non-test source file; BUILD-only test edits are classified with tests. Mixed infrastructure has precedence. Definitions differ from the prior report; no causal before/after estimate.

CheckType ALL retains attempts; suite/run page completion verified. One selected head has no exact-head PR workflow in the window and is excluded. Historical synthetic merge trees were separately recovered for inspected cases.

Workflow creation proxies push time. Green means latest successful results in all three current required contexts. Draft, review, conflicts and mergeability history are not reconstructed; actual auto-merge readiness is unobserved.

Collection is non-atomic. Current draft/mergeable state is not historical eligibility. Fork trust delays may predate the first linked workflow. Cached/fresh and small/large path mixtures remain within classes.

devel_pod_concurrency.decision: Four Pod case slots landed through PR #16659. In its frozen unsplit 22-case cohort, all cases passed and mean action time fell from 363.3s to 289.2s (20.4%); the case envelope fell 29.8%. Pod requests, memory limits and executor sizing stayed fixed. The current required inventory is partitioned differently, so this is not a new port measurement.
devel_pod_concurrency.scope: Two fresh actions per setting, sequential order 2/4/4/2, with all 88 JUnit case executions passing. Input trees, executor properties and case identities are identical; decoded Commands differ only in the case-limit environment variable. All fixtures were distinct, infrastructure was warm, and cleanup completed. Mean setup was 35.2s at two slots and 40.4s at four; setup variation is separate from case concurrency. This small action screen does not establish whole-PR savings, p90, cold-start behavior or a fleet reliability rate. Two-slot action times ranged 335.6–391.1s; four-slot times ranged 285.2–293.1s. One trust probe took 94.5s in the slower control versus 12–17s elsewhere; its wait is not subdivided in existing traces, so that outlier is not attributed to concurrency. Against the faster control alone, the four-slot mean is 13.8% shorter; this is a sensitivity comparison, not a confidence bound.
devel_pod_concurrency.memory_finding: Maximum whole-action memory was 5.07 GiB at two slots and 5.12 GiB at four. Kubelet samples retained at least 4.51 GiB available and sampled up to 5 runtime Pods in the four-slot arm. Before-import/final snapshots contain no FailedScheduling, OOMKilled or eviction reasons. Ten-second sampling and snapshots can miss transient events.

required_ci.scope: Independent exact-head PR acceptance, not one of the four matched performance actions.

case_duration_variation.cause: Unknown: existing case/scenario spans do not subdivide the trust probe waits. Do not attribute this outlier to the slot count.

pod_concurrency.decision: This frozen fifteen-case App Pod screen compared two, three and four workers with Pod requests, memory limits, outer executor sizing and case ownership fixed. The four-worker default is now on devel; these are historical measurements at the linked benchmark source.
pod_concurrency.scope: Two uncached actions per setting, ordered 2/3/4 then 4/3/2. All 90 JUnit case executions passed. Identical input trees and executor properties; Commands differ only by the case-limit environment variable. Infrastructure was warm, fixtures were distinct, and cleanup completed. This is an action screen, not complete PR feedback or a fleet failure-rate estimate. Control setup averaged 17 seconds slower than four-worker setup, so the full 21.4% action difference cannot all be attributed to concurrency; the case envelope fell 23.6%.
pod_concurrency.memory_finding: No memory setting changed. Maximum whole-action memory was 4.95 GiB at two workers, 4.99 at three and 4.87 at four. Kubelet samples retained at least about 4.70 GiB available and sampled up to five concurrent runtime Pods in the four-worker arm. Before-import/final snapshots contain no FailedScheduling, OOMKilled or eviction reasons. Ten-second sampling and final snapshots can miss transient events.

backend.method: Nearest-rank percentiles among successful exact heads. Start: earliest observed pull_request workflow creation for that head. End: latest visible successful completion of all three currently required contexts. Latest check IDs determine each context’s outcome. Same-head repeated attempts can use different synthetic merge trees; they are not automatically same-source test recoveries or flakes. The non-atomic API observation completed 13 November 03:04:30 UTC; a subsequent analysis restricted base branches without refetching those records.

lanes.title: Recover completed RBE results after execution-stream loss
lanes.status: Recovery control complete; diagnostic PR open
lanes.observed: Native Bazel recovered one injected gRPC INTERNAL after its first Operation using one Execute and one same-ID WaitExecution. Two interruptions exhausted remote_retries=1: one physical test passed, but Bazel exited 34 with no TestResult. This is a sufficient false-red mechanism, not proof of the natural RST_STREAM cause.
lanes.measurement: Next natural false-red: private narrowly enabled native remote_grpc_log; summarize first Operation, Execute/WaitExecution statuses and retry consumption, correlate exact provider operation. Separate Wait-only retry budget is an upstream candidate requiring cancellation/Execute replay controls.
lanes.acceptance: Capture the native Execute/WaitExecution sequence and inject a transport reset after the first accepted Operation. Verify recovery of the original result, one physical execution, a native TestResult, and cancellation behavior. Correlate provider/proxy traces where available. Keep remote_retries=1 until cancellation safety is demonstrated; keep raw RPC metadata private.

lanes.title: Validate KVM placement for required Agentplane VM CI
lanes.status: Capacity evidence merged; routing unchanged
lanes.observed: Seven physical actions / 31 JUnit cases passed. Four KVM actions shared three registered slots; the fourth queued 215.314s and finished 66.668s after the managed VM. Pod finished last, giving zero VM-only fixed-clock headroom. The newer-source repeat is not a matched graph.
lanes.measurement: Run at least three bounded bursts, each equivalent to four concurrent PRs, on literal source pins. Include one after natural scale-down to one registered worker; observe all required GitHub gates and isolation.
lanes.acceptance: Repeat matched cold/warm selected graphs and bounded concurrent admission on the existing pool, recording routing, compatible healthy/busy capacity, queue clocks, source/CAS identity, cleanup and all ordinary VM cases. Obtain actual required-check feedback on the experiment PR. Propose required routing only when complete feedback and capacity evidence support it.

lanes.title: Eliminate avoidable cold Agentplane system-test baseline rebuilds
lanes.status: Reason diagnostic merged; cache repair unproven
lanes.observed: The 12-head census found 36 target opportunities: 18 absent, three unavailable, three cached and 12 fresh suite outcomes, with 15 unique physical IDs. Six of 12 fresh baselines were cold; all cleaned up. Old artifacts did not record why. The merged span records reuse/rebuild reasons without retaining extra mutable state.
lanes.measurement: Collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh retained-suite outcomes, whichever is later. Keep cached, failed and missing outcomes separate; group by backend, worker, compatibility key, fingerprint and rebuild reason.
lanes.acceptance: Measure natural cold/warm exposure, baseline fingerprints and explicit rebuild reasons. Repair avoidable compatibility-key or retention misses supported by evidence. Preserve fresh namespace, database, root/credentials and workspace identities with certified cleanup. Evaluate probe cadence only with full-case and CPU evidence.

lanes.title: Skip unchanged OCI imports only when the image is usable
lanes.status: Usability guard and warm trial pass; draft PR
lanes.observed: Nine real native usability guard cases passed. Same-worker warm ABBA setup averaged 46.992s control versus 32.216s candidate, 14.776s shorter. Both selected graphs passed the identical 27 cases. Their 458.570s / 472.642s Bazel times are not causal evidence: VM root-image inputs differed and order/cache exposure were unmatched.
lanes.measurement: Keep issue #16028 open. Within seven days after merge or on the next naturally selected backend head, compare matched warm/cold complete graphs and exact-head required gates. Record source/CAS and cache identities, native phases, CPU, peak memory and capacity. Resolve the VM generated-root input mismatch before comparing VM results.
lanes.acceptance: Implement or experimentally reject an import fast path guarded by exact manifest target, correct-platform unpacked filesystem and CRI pin. Exercise same tag/new digest, missing unpack/pin, GC, restart and later Sandbox use. Measure counterbalanced warm/cold lifecycle and selected-graph behavior; source blobs alone are insufficient.

lanes.title: Shorten MCP Actions execution with isolated case resources
lanes.status: Case overlap measured; no action saving
lanes.observed: All five real MCP cases passed in each source-matched ABBA arm. Mean case envelope fell from 112.336s to 96.833s, but whole action grew from 254.348s to 265.866s and CPU also rose. Baselines were warm/warm/warm/cold across different workers. Five peak Sandboxes exactly fit the existing cap; no action, compute or CI win is established.
lanes.measurement: After adoption, collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh MCP executions, whichever is later. Compare case execution, setup, CPU, scheduling and the last required gate, with cache, retry, baseline-state and tested-source groups kept separate.
lanes.acceptance: Use existing spans to identify the binding phase. Test case-owned OAuth linkage/resources to overlap independent variants, preserving actual login/linkage/tool behavior, the Sandbox cap, cleanup and unique identities. Compare full selected graphs and required CI rather than raising concurrency blindly.

lanes.title: Test read-only harness artifact mounts to avoid OCI unpacking
lanes.status: Real mount feasibility passed; manual draft PR
lanes.observed: Claude and Codex each completed instructed and plain turns in fresh Sandboxes with 44 read-only native artifact mounts and fresh writable homes; cleanup passed. Declared inputs total 914,451,230 bytes versus 914,498,274 packaged, only 47,044 bytes less. One unmatched pair observed less unpack/setup work, but no meaningful input-byte saving or causal CI gain.
lanes.measurement: Keep issue #16030 open. On the next relevant backend head or within seven days of the feasibility pass, compare counterbalanced complete Pod/MCP/VM graphs while retaining real packaged-image boot coverage. Match source/CAS and cache exposure; measure required gates, per-Sandbox mounts, lazy artifact reads and resource cost.
lanes.acceptance: Build a manual real-runtime experiment using pinned declared artifacts, exact paths and executable permissions, fresh writable homes/state and existing isolation. Retain a required real image packaging/boot path. Include RBE input transfer and complete setup/case/cleanup costs; reject the design if those costs or boundary constraints defeat it.

lanes.title: Diagnose and repair silent progress loss in VM CI guests
lanes.status: New QEMU crash classified; original stall unresolved
lanes.observed: A fresh natural failure aborted QEMU at guest uptime 1.773s with an iotlb_to_section assertion; replacement scenario passed but original shutdown receipt was missing. Separate issue #16057 tracks the crash. Two fresh VM passes used three physical actions because one provider pause failed. The original 300s admitted-turn stall did not recur; late live triggers remain unexercised.
lanes.measurement: On the next admitted-turn stall, correlate live samples at 210 and 240 seconds for the same Sandbox UID with Runtime history and independent serial output before cleanup. Review seven days of non-cached physical exposure; the original stall remains open.
lanes.acceptance: Inspect new physical failure artifacts and a comparable pass; attempt a bounded faithful reproduction. Trace the first blocked native operation and repair an established mechanism with a regression. If lifecycle ownership is implicated, map shutdown/reconciliation and simplify one race-tested path. Do not raise timeouts for a wedge.

lanes.title: Diagnose and repair browser login fixture stalls
lanes.status: Controlled auth timeout localized; natural cause open
lanes.observed: Three fresh browser cases passed with six successful auth exchanges (40–131ms). Holding actual TLS OIDC discovery for 5.25s caused AppProcess.authenticate to time out after 5.002s before page interaction, with client, Go and provider phases retained. This faithful hop control does not reproduce the unknown natural cause or show a lower failure rate.
lanes.measurement: Next natural failure: join client trace ID to Go phases and provider path/port to locate first missing hop; seven-day count of non-cached physical setup outcomes, separate cached rows.
lanes.acceptance: Correlate current failure artifacts client → Go app → provider and find the first missing phase; use a bounded targeted reproduction and repair the responsible boundary. Reuse existing logging, preserve real session issuance/OIDC behavior and token/cookie redaction, without generic retries or timeout bumps.

lanes.title: Locate and repair browser history projection lag
lanes.status: Route-lifetime repair and evidence retention merged
lanes.observed: New natural failure had committed/direct/fresh Electric cursor 334 versus DOM 264; its final live GET began 2.298ms after last-route removal. The repair retains the released route until page cleanup and fixes binary-telemetry request classification. Final candidate passed ten fresh physical stream cases, preserving cursor/anchor/draft assertions. Natural recurrence reduction remains unmeasured.
lanes.measurement: Seven days of post-change physical exposure and next natural failure: final request compared with port-specific ingress and Chromium timing; upstream admission determines next owner.
lanes.acceptance: Correlate committed/direct view, fresh Electric snapshot, browser stream/CDP and DOM cursor on fresh failures. Use the first divergent boundary for a deterministic regression and repair while retaining real streaming integration. Preserve immutable per-attempt artifacts so later diagnostics cannot overwrite the causal evidence.

lanes.title: Refresh backend CI cohort and publish ten-lane follow-up measurements
lanes.status: Fresh cohort and both reports prepared
lanes.observed: 159 latest devel-base backend heads include 129 production heads: 124 green, four failed, one cancelled. Green feedback mean is 13m36s, median 11m27s, p90 23m38s. All 24 repeated green heads had earlier failed Bazel checks and account for 43.1% of summed head feedback. This pre-dispatch baseline is not an attributed improvement.
lanes.measurement: After the dispatched changes land, collect seven complete UTC days (extend sparse lane samples to their stated thresholds), keeping cached, missing, cancelled and failed outcomes separate. Recompute exact-head required feedback and fresh physical failure exposure against this pre-dispatch baseline; link the report PR and each result in issue #16034.
lanes.acceptance: Refresh paginated backend PR-head required-check feedback and reliability exposure; verify current rules, tested merge provenance, native outcomes and repeat attempts. Publish reviewed latency/reliability reports through a gh-pages PR with rendered desktop/mobile/light/dark validation and links to all lane tracking issues.

backend.method: Nearest-rank percentiles among successful exact heads. Start: earliest observed pull_request workflow creation for that head. End: latest visible successful completion of all three currently required contexts. Latest check IDs determine each context’s outcome. Same-head repeated attempts can use different synthetic merge trees; they are not automatically same-source test recoveries or flakes. The non-atomic API observation completed 13 November 03:04:30 UTC; a subsequent analysis restricted base branches without refetching those records.

lanes.title: Recover completed RBE results after execution-stream loss
lanes.status: Recovery control complete; diagnostic PR open
lanes.observed: Native Bazel recovered one injected gRPC INTERNAL after its first Operation using one Execute and one same-ID WaitExecution. Two interruptions exhausted remote_retries=1: one physical test passed, but Bazel exited 34 with no TestResult. This is a sufficient false-red mechanism, not proof of the natural RST_STREAM cause.
lanes.measurement: Next natural false-red: private narrowly enabled native remote_grpc_log; summarize first Operation, Execute/WaitExecution statuses and retry consumption, correlate exact provider operation. Separate Wait-only retry budget is an upstream candidate requiring cancellation/Execute replay controls.
lanes.acceptance: Capture the native Execute/WaitExecution sequence and inject a transport reset after the first accepted Operation. Verify recovery of the original result, one physical execution, a native TestResult, and cancellation behavior. Correlate provider/proxy traces where available. Keep remote_retries=1 until cancellation safety is demonstrated; keep raw RPC metadata private.

lanes.title: Validate KVM placement for required Agentplane VM CI
lanes.status: Capacity evidence merged; routing unchanged
lanes.observed: Seven physical actions / 31 JUnit cases passed. Four KVM actions shared three registered slots; the fourth queued 215.314s and finished 66.668s after the managed VM. Pod finished last, giving zero VM-only fixed-clock headroom. The newer-source repeat is not a matched graph.
lanes.measurement: Run at least three bounded bursts, each equivalent to four concurrent PRs, on literal source pins. Include one after natural scale-down to one registered worker; observe all required GitHub gates and isolation.
lanes.acceptance: Repeat matched cold/warm selected graphs and bounded concurrent admission on the existing pool, recording routing, compatible healthy/busy capacity, queue clocks, source/CAS identity, cleanup and all ordinary VM cases. Obtain actual required-check feedback on the experiment PR. Propose required routing only when complete feedback and capacity evidence support it.

lanes.title: Eliminate avoidable cold Agentplane system-test baseline rebuilds
lanes.status: Reason diagnostic merged; cache repair unproven
lanes.observed: The 12-head census found 36 target opportunities: 18 absent, three unavailable, three cached and 12 fresh suite outcomes, with 15 unique physical IDs. Six of 12 fresh baselines were cold; all cleaned up. Old artifacts did not record why. The merged span records reuse/rebuild reasons without retaining extra mutable state.
lanes.measurement: Collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh retained-suite outcomes, whichever is later. Keep cached, failed and missing outcomes separate; group by backend, worker, compatibility key, fingerprint and rebuild reason.
lanes.acceptance: Measure natural cold/warm exposure, baseline fingerprints and explicit rebuild reasons. Repair avoidable compatibility-key or retention misses supported by evidence. Preserve fresh namespace, database, root/credentials and workspace identities with certified cleanup. Evaluate probe cadence only with full-case and CPU evidence.

lanes.title: Skip unchanged OCI imports only when the image is usable
lanes.status: Usability guard and warm trial pass; draft PR
lanes.observed: Nine real native usability guard cases passed. Same-worker warm ABBA setup averaged 46.992s control versus 32.216s candidate, 14.776s shorter. Both selected graphs passed the identical 27 cases. Their 458.570s / 472.642s Bazel times are not causal evidence: VM root-image inputs differed and order/cache exposure were unmatched.
lanes.measurement: Keep issue #16028 open. Within seven days after merge or on the next naturally selected backend head, compare matched warm/cold complete graphs and exact-head required gates. Record source/CAS and cache identities, native phases, CPU, peak memory and capacity. Resolve the VM generated-root input mismatch before comparing VM results.
lanes.acceptance: Implement or experimentally reject an import fast path guarded by exact manifest target, correct-platform unpacked filesystem and CRI pin. Exercise same tag/new digest, missing unpack/pin, GC, restart and later Sandbox use. Measure counterbalanced warm/cold lifecycle and selected-graph behavior; source blobs alone are insufficient.

lanes.title: Shorten MCP Actions execution with isolated case resources
lanes.status: Case overlap measured; no action saving
lanes.observed: All five real MCP cases passed in each source-matched ABBA arm. Mean case envelope fell from 112.336s to 96.833s, but whole action grew from 254.348s to 265.866s and CPU also rose. Baselines were warm/warm/warm/cold across different workers. Five peak Sandboxes exactly fit the existing cap; no action, compute or CI win is established.
lanes.measurement: After adoption, collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh MCP executions, whichever is later. Compare case execution, setup, CPU, scheduling and the last required gate, with cache, retry, baseline-state and tested-source groups kept separate.
lanes.acceptance: Use existing spans to identify the binding phase. Test case-owned OAuth linkage/resources to overlap independent variants, preserving actual login/linkage/tool behavior, the Sandbox cap, cleanup and unique identities. Compare full selected graphs and required CI rather than raising concurrency blindly.

lanes.title: Test read-only harness artifact mounts to avoid OCI unpacking
lanes.status: Real mount feasibility passed; manual draft PR
lanes.observed: Claude and Codex each completed instructed and plain turns in fresh Sandboxes with 44 read-only native artifact mounts and fresh writable homes; cleanup passed. Declared inputs total 914,451,230 bytes versus 914,498,274 packaged, only 47,044 bytes less. One unmatched pair observed less unpack/setup work, but no meaningful input-byte saving or causal CI gain.
lanes.measurement: Keep issue #16030 open. On the next relevant backend head or within seven days of the feasibility pass, compare counterbalanced complete Pod/MCP/VM graphs while retaining real packaged-image boot coverage. Match source/CAS and cache exposure; measure required gates, per-Sandbox mounts, lazy artifact reads and resource cost.
lanes.acceptance: Build a manual real-runtime experiment using pinned declared artifacts, exact paths and executable permissions, fresh writable homes/state and existing isolation. Retain a required real image packaging/boot path. Include RBE input transfer and complete setup/case/cleanup costs; reject the design if those costs or boundary constraints defeat it.

lanes.title: Diagnose and repair silent progress loss in VM CI guests
lanes.status: New QEMU crash classified; original stall unresolved
lanes.observed: A fresh natural failure aborted QEMU at guest uptime 1.773s with an iotlb_to_section assertion; replacement scenario passed but original shutdown receipt was missing. Separate issue #16057 tracks the crash. Two fresh VM passes used three physical actions because one provider pause failed. The original 300s admitted-turn stall did not recur; late live triggers remain unexercised.
lanes.measurement: On the next admitted-turn stall, correlate live samples at 210 and 240 seconds for the same Sandbox UID with Runtime history and independent serial output before cleanup. Review seven days of non-cached physical exposure; the original stall remains open.
lanes.acceptance: Inspect new physical failure artifacts and a comparable pass; attempt a bounded faithful reproduction. Trace the first blocked native operation and repair an established mechanism with a regression. If lifecycle ownership is implicated, map shutdown/reconciliation and simplify one race-tested path. Do not raise timeouts for a wedge.

lanes.title: Diagnose and repair browser login fixture stalls
lanes.status: Controlled auth timeout localized; natural cause open
lanes.observed: Three fresh browser cases passed with six successful auth exchanges (40–131ms). Holding actual TLS OIDC discovery for 5.25s caused AppProcess.authenticate to time out after 5.002s before page interaction, with client, Go and provider phases retained. This faithful hop control does not reproduce the unknown natural cause or show a lower failure rate.
lanes.measurement: Next natural failure: join client trace ID to Go phases and provider path/port to locate first missing hop; seven-day count of non-cached physical setup outcomes, separate cached rows.
lanes.acceptance: Correlate current failure artifacts client → Go app → provider and find the first missing phase; use a bounded targeted reproduction and repair the responsible boundary. Reuse existing logging, preserve real session issuance/OIDC behavior and token/cookie redaction, without generic retries or timeout bumps.

lanes.title: Locate and repair browser history projection lag
lanes.status: Route-lifetime repair and evidence retention merged
lanes.observed: New natural failure had committed/direct/fresh Electric cursor 334 versus DOM 264; its final live GET began 2.298ms after last-route removal. The repair retains the released route until page cleanup and fixes binary-telemetry request classification. Final candidate passed ten fresh physical stream cases, preserving cursor/anchor/draft assertions. Natural recurrence reduction remains unmeasured.
lanes.measurement: Seven days of post-change physical exposure and next natural failure: final request compared with port-specific ingress and Chromium timing; upstream admission determines next owner.
lanes.acceptance: Correlate committed/direct view, fresh Electric snapshot, browser stream/CDP and DOM cursor on fresh failures. Use the first divergent boundary for a deterministic regression and repair while retaining real streaming integration. Preserve immutable per-attempt artifacts so later diagnostics cannot overwrite the causal evidence.

lanes.title: Refresh backend CI cohort and publish ten-lane follow-up measurements
lanes.status: Fresh cohort and both reports prepared
lanes.observed: 159 latest devel-base backend heads include 129 production heads: 124 green, four failed, one cancelled. Green feedback mean is 13m36s, median 11m27s, p90 23m38s. All 24 repeated green heads had earlier failed Bazel checks and account for 43.1% of summed head feedback. This pre-dispatch baseline is not an attributed improvement.
lanes.measurement: After the dispatched changes land, collect seven complete UTC days (extend sparse lane samples to their stated thresholds), keeping cached, missing, cancelled and failed outcomes separate. Recompute exact-head required feedback and fresh physical failure exposure against this pre-dispatch baseline; link the report PR and each result in issue #16034.
lanes.acceptance: Refresh paginated backend PR-head required-check feedback and reliability exposure; verify current rules, tested merge provenance, native outcomes and repeat attempts. Publish reviewed latency/reliability reports through a gh-pages PR with rendered desktop/mobile/light/dark validation and links to all lane tracking issues.

vm_kvm_qualification.status: Functional pass; latency routing qualification not met
vm_kvm_qualification.decision: Keep required VM tests on their current managed lane. Both real harness cases pass on the existing shared KVM pool, but shared-pool admission waits outweigh the process-time benefit in the observed selected-graph comparisons. The merged maximum of eight is capacity permission; the unchanged slow scale-up policy does not supply eight registered workers at burst arrival. This live pool was not reserved, so background occupancy is part of the observed result rather than a controlled variable.
vm_kvm_qualification.workload: Three candidate bursts and two complete controls; each arm runs four VM actions, four Firecracker actions and four single native/App straggler witnesses. A third control was interrupted by the outer service time cap and is retained separately. This is synthetic four-PR-equivalent KVM demand, not four complete PR gates.
vm_kvm_qualification.comparison_boundary: Same pinned source, labels, tests, images and full CAS input roots were checked per run. This compares the configured production managed lane (8 compute units / 16-vCPU entitlement, retained K3s baseline) with the existing KVM lane (4-vCPU / 8-GiB worker, 4-CPU / 7-GiB scheduler estimate, fresh Docker/K3s). Hardware, isolation and reuse differ together. It does not isolate a pure KVM speedup. Managed warm and cold actions are retained separately. Candidate then control order is fixed, capacity changes between arms, and the live pool is shared with other work; queue differences are not a randomized causal estimate.
vm_kvm_qualification.feedback_boundary: Bazel command elapsed is start-to-finish for the six selected labels, including build/cache analysis. Queue is workerStartTimestamp minus queuedTimestamp; worker preparation and process are separate native execution intervals. Negative/missing clocks remain unknown. No GitHub workflow, push-to-feedback, auto-merge or measured fleet improvement is inferred. Only three candidate command observations and two controls; p90 is the maximum at these sample sizes. Registered start/end values use the last returned 15-second sample within 30 seconds of each boundary.

native_guest_console.known_qemu_inventory_gap: The early collector comm filter omitted qemu-kvm before 12:45:30 UTC; empty arrays in that interval do not establish absence.

prometheus.coverage_note: Prometheus points are retained only where returned. Empty or missing series are unknown unless the recorded query returned an explicit vector(0) fallback.

known_capacity_context.provenance: Operator-provided observation; VM CPU request/limit and memory are crosschecked in pool snapshots.
known_capacity_context.scale_up_limit: At most one additional replica per 900 seconds.
known_capacity_context.scaling_control: Autoscaler-managed; no manual replica changes were made during this observation.

limits_and_interpretation: Prometheus resource data ends at its last returned sample; no claim extends to later console samples or pool snapshots.
CPU and PSI Prometheus series are rate queries with a 3-minute lookback window; short spikes are smoothed and the first boundary sample can depend on pre-window samples.
OOM and swap counter increments are computed only between observed samples in the requested window; resets are counted and post-reset values are included. They are not lifetime totals.

Native memory.peak is the maximum observed sample from mapped buildbuddy-exec-* cgroups. The sampling interval is about 5 seconds, so it can miss the action's true final or instantaneous peak; the executor container is excluded.

The early native QEMU collector comm filter omitted qemu-kvm before 12:45:30 UTC. Empty qemu arrays in that interval are not evidence that no QEMU process existed; separate shutdown artifacts provide independent evidence.
Pool snapshots are point-in-time files, sorted by file modification time. They can postdate the Prometheus range.

action_parent_cgroup_memory_peak.interpretation: Maximum sampled memory.peak among Docker containers mapped to buildbuddy-exec-* action parents; this is an observed maximum and may miss the final 5-second sample or later peak. The executor container is excluded.

action_parent_memory_events.interpretation: memory.events counters are sampled from mapped buildbuddy-exec-* action-parent cgroups only. The collector reads memory.events, not memory.events.local, so the summary does not distinguish parent-local events from descendant events. Initial positive values are reported as baselines, not increments; reset baselines are also excluded from deltas. Missing fields and files are counted separately from zero-valued observations.

action_parent_memory_max.interpretation: Sampled action-parent cgroup memory.max values; 'unlimited' reflects the literal cgroup value 'max'. Distribution counts may include a cgroup in more than one value if its limit changed.

actual_kvm_qemu.identity_output: Counts only; no process IDs, cgroup IDs, container names, worker names, or command lines are emitted.

registered_desired_busy_and_local_reserv.local_reservations_meaning: Executor-local queue-length metric summed from worker pods; it is not central BuildBuddy backlog.

oom_kills.increment_semantics: positive deltas; on reset, add the post-reset counter value

pages_swapped_in.increment_semantics: positive deltas; on reset, add the post-reset counter value

pages_swapped_out.increment_semantics: positive deltas; on reset, add the post-reset counter value

resources.native_host_physical_memory_and_psi: Not sampled by the guest console collector; use the Prometheus host series above.

prometheus_host_oom_kills.increment_semantics: positive deltas; on reset, add the post-reset counter value

vm_kvm_qualification.admission_mechanism: Registered capacity grew from one to 5 during the observation, rather than starting at the configured maximum eight. Scale-up still waits through a 120-second stabilization window and permits only one added VM per 900 seconds. Worker creation-to-Ready took 172, 176 and 187 seconds for the first three additions. Registration health is a separate prerequisite; requested replicas are not usable slots. Missing/unregistered workers retain desired capacity in the demand proxy. Executor-local reservations can duplicate a task across workers and are not scheduler-wide queue depth.

vm_kvm_qualification.resource_summary: The observed RAM envelope has a sampled action peak of 5.77 GiB inside an 8-GiB VM and as little as 1.09 GiB guest memory available. No OOM kill or swap activity was observed, but subtree memory.events:max counters increased; unlimited parent memory.max does not rule out a constrained descendant. Keep guest RAM unchanged. The first cohosted pair demonstrates operation with host spread disabled, not the full eight-worker fleet. Exact memory, CPU, disk, PSI, OOM and sampling gaps remain in evidence.json; scheduler estimates and requests are not measured demand. Native collection retained 2299 samples and discarded 2 malformed serial records; maximum interior gap 12.279s. Worker streams start and stop at different times, so missing endpoints are not covered by that interior-gap statistic.
vm_kvm_qualification.next_action: Next narrow intervention: qualify faster admission while preserving the eight-worker ceiling, metric freshness/registration guard and cleanup ownership. Measure cold-start arrival, scale-up, matched warm-start four-PR bursts, existing Firecracker latency and scale-down/drain before revisiting routing. Changing the scale-up policy is a separate deployment decision; this experiment changed no deployed autoscaling or required routing.
methods: Source pin 425fb8cab9a062f42a29ddc85079af4feedf155b. Every arm used --config=rbe --config=ci --nocache_test_results --flaky_test_attempts=1 --runs_per_test=1, with label-specific --runs_per_test=...:test_vm@4 and ...:test_firecracker@4. All four single-run witnesses retain their original execution route. Target cache was disabled; build/input caches were deliberately left enabled.

Selected labels: //agentplane/system_tests/suites:test_vm, :test_firecracker, :test_pod, :test_pod_platform, :test_dispatcher and //agentplane/system_tests/suites/mcp:test_gateway_budget. The production test_vm label was temporarily given exactly the existing manual KVM target platform and AGENTPLANE_K3S_REQUIRE_KVM=1 in the private remote experiment. Each control uses the original BUILD. The last control was interrupted in the ephemeral remote workspace; no source commit, deployed routing or workflow was changed.

Raw BES TestResult, JUnit XML, GetExecution NEW physical actions, native fixture spans, persistence receipts, host-QEMU/topology artifacts, native guest/cgroup counters and Mimir queries are separate evidence layers. Inner K3s pod working sets are not outer action memory. The native executor omits outer usageStats CPU/peak memory; those remain unknown rather than zero, with sampled parent-cgroup peaks supplied separately.

Input identity uses SHA-256-verified native CAS Action and Command messages and whole input-root Merkle digests, compared by TEST_RUN_NUMBER. Normalization removes the platform and intentional KVM flag/test-run variable only. Raw Commands, credentials, worker/container identities, guest logs and full API payloads remain private. Public records contain reviewed digests, clocks, verdicts and nonidentifying resource aggregates.

Per-action p50/p90 use nearest rank; means are arithmetic. Only valid clock intervals enter summaries; inverted clocks are counted. Concurrent cases use first start to last end, not the sum of overlapping spans. Warm/cold receipt outcomes are stratified in the downloadable evidence. There are twelve candidate VM observations, eight complete control VM observations, three candidate commands, two control commands and only one cold-start pool ramp.

Historical 12 November cold managed 4-CPU comparison (346.448 vs 219.986 seconds) is retained as prior evidence, not used as the expectation for today’s production 8-compute-unit warm-baseline lane. The existing 10–16 November PR cohort has not been recollected by this experiment; its original window and source remain explicit below.

Descendant-local memory attribution was attempted with a bounded serial-console probe, but command delivery failed and no descendant_inventory samples were collected. The max-event owner remains unknown. This diagnostic is not a passing resource check. All qualification actions reached terminal physical index states; the interrupted control was not replayed.
